subject: Future Tech
title: Additive vs Subtractive
description: A quick, practical guide to Additive vs Subtractive.

hook.text: Traditional manufacturing carves objects by removing material. A sculptor chisels marble away.

buildup.text: CNC machines mill metal blocks into parts by cutting away excess.

discovery.text: 3D printing uses only the material needed for the object plus minimal support structures.

twist.text: But additive manufacturing is slower per part.

climax.text: The sweet spot is low-volume, high-complexity parts where customization matters more than speed.

punchline.text: Adding material is wasteless. Subtracting it is not.

quiz.question: How much material waste can CNC machining produce?
